root_cause.text: The `last_gc` timestamp was being updated unconditionally on every connection tracking operation, rather than only when garbage collection was actually performed, allowing high packet rates to indefinitely defer GC execution and cause unbounded list growth.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the `list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;` assignment from the end of the function (line 251, executed for every new connection added) to inside the garbage collection conditional block (line 232, executed only when GC actually runs). This ensures the GC timeout is only reset when garbage collection has genuinely occurred, preventing attackers from bypassing GC through sustained high packet rates.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit FIXES the vulnerability rather than introducing it. The root cause was that `last_gc` was being updated unconditionally on every operation, deferring GC indefinitely. This commit implements the correct fix by: (1) Only updating `last_gc` when GC is actually performed - see line 271 where `list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;` is placed AFTER garbage collection logic completes, and line 197 where it's updated after adding a node; (2) Adding early exit checks using `time_is_after_eq_jiffies()` at lines 135-136 in `__nf_conncount_add()` and lines 236-237 in `nf_conncount_gc_list()` to prevent unnecessary GC attempts within the same jiffie; (3) Initializing `last_gc` properly at line 222. The fix ensures GC is throttled to at most once per jiffie, preventing the unbounded list growth caused by high packet rates continuously deferring GC. This is a Bug-Fixing Commit, not a Bug-Introducing Commit.
